**Seeding complete — 7 sealed single-fault variants.**

**Variants completed: 7** (`arms/variants/bug01` … `bug07`). Each is a self-buildable copy of the chess sources with its own `zxtap.py`, `Makefile` and `BUILD.md` carrying the exact build line; each assembles cleanly with `pasmo` and reproduces its committed `chess.tap` byte for byte. Every variant's assembled binary differs from pristine in exactly one byte, and all seven trees are identical in file list, sizes and mtimes. Every fault was verified to manifest through the emulator (position/move sequence → observed vs expected, recorded in the key), and each has an acceptance check that was run twice — exit 1 on the seeded build, exit 0 once the fault is undone.

**sha256 of `sealed/answer_key.json`:**
`27d47c88136107f0e9c2f236de85b0ba7cf2cc4e92d8ccdea19c8de72d0ebd2f`

**Bug reports** (`bug_reports/`, symptom-level only):

| file | symptom |
|---|---|
| `bug01.md` | the engine's evaluation readout is far too optimistic, and it plays for phantom material |
| `bug02.md` | the game is declared a 50-move draw two moves after a pawn was pushed |
| `bug03.md` | promoting to a rook gives a queen, and promoting to a knight gives a bishop |
| `bug04.md` | the engine leaves free pieces on the board and thinks it is winning when it is lost |
| `bug05.md` | a rook reappears on a1 out of nowhere once the rook that started there has moved away |
| `bug06.md` | the strength setting does nothing: levels 3, 4 and 5 return the level-2 answer |
| `bug07.md` | checkmate is announced as "Stalemate - draw" |

**Harness caveats** (`arms/harness/`, hc91emu without `chess/` and without `.git`; `HOWTO.md` documents all of this):

- **Give each arm only its own variant directory.** The trees are deliberately indistinguishable, so diffing two variants against each other would expose both faults instantly.
- Trimmed of `tests/out`, `tests/vectors`, `dist`, `software`, `game-wip*` (1.2 GB → 5.4 MB). Build with `make build/hc91emu`, not `make test` — the emulator's own vector tests need data that was not copied. A prebuilt binary and `roms/48.rom` are included; a variant tap was verified to boot, play and pass `make test` from its own directory.
- Building a variant needs `pasmo` and `python3`.
- Two bug-neutral tools were added for this lane: `tools/chesspos.py` (inject any FEN — including castling rights, en-passant square and halfmove clock — by appending a 71-byte block to `chess.tap` and pressing the game's own tape-load key `L`; also decodes a `.sna` back to FEN plus game state) and `tools/play.py` (one command per session).
- The screen OCR (`--text`) cannot read the piece glyphs — they come out as `?`. Read the board from a snapshot instead; the right-hand text panel (`Level`/`Move`/`Eval`/`Matl`/clocks/status) *is* readable.
- Two timing quirks that will silently corrupt a hand-written repro: the strength keys `1`–`5` set both sides' search depth while a tape load only restores White's, and a loaded position with Black to move goes straight to the engine — so press the digit and `V` *before* `L`. Give each move its own `--type` a few hundred frames apart, since keystrokes arriving during a screen repaint or an engine search are dropped. `play.py` handles both.
- Each side has a 5:00 (15000-frame) clock and the engine spends about 1/32 of its remaining time per move, so long scripted sessions can end in a flag-fall.
